text: Mainly because they offer things supermarkets can't. The produce is often fresher, since it comes straight from farms, and you can talk to the person who actually grew it. There's also a price advantage for seasonal fruit and vegetables. And for many people, especially older ones, going to the market is a social habit — they've known the same sellers for decades.

tips.en: Fresher, There's also and And give three reasons, each with a new linker.
tips.kk: Fresher … There's also … And — үш себеп, әрқайсысы жаңа байланыстырушы сөзбен.
tips.ru: Fresher … There's also … And — три причины, каждая с новой связкой.

tips.en: A social habit is a less obvious reason that adds depth.
tips.kk: A social habit — күтпеген себеп жауапты тереңірек етеді.
tips.ru: A social habit — неочевидная причина делает ответ глубже.
tips.example: going to the market is a social habit

note.en: “Directly from the people who grow it”.

questions.followUp: Will they survive another twenty years?
questions.question: Why do traditional markets still survive when there are so many supermarkets?

text: I think it can be, as long as both sides are relaxed about it. For buyers, it's a chance to get a fair price, and for sellers, it's a way of building a relationship with regular customers. The problem is tourists, who often don't know the real price and end up paying three times as much. In that case, fixed prices would honestly be fairer.

tips.en: As long as both sides are relaxed about it means “yes, on one condition”.
tips.kk: As long as both sides are relaxed about it — «иә, бірақ шартпен».
tips.ru: As long as both sides are relaxed about it — «да, но при условии».
tips.example: as long as both sides are relaxed about it

tips.en: For buyers and for sellers answer both parts of the question.
tips.kk: For buyers … for sellers — сұрақта екі жақ бар, екеуіне де жауап берілді.
tips.ru: For buyers … for sellers — в вопросе две стороны, и обе получили ответ.
tips.example: For buyers, it's a chance to get a fair price

questions.question: Is bargaining a good thing for buyers and sellers?

text: Yes, I'm in favour of that. At the moment, a lot of the money goes to middlemen, so farmers earn very little even when food prices in shops are high. Governments could provide cheap stalls in city markets or help farmers set up online shops. It would keep rural communities alive and give city people healthier, cheaper food, so everyone would benefit.

tips.en: A lot of the money goes to middlemen explains why help is needed.
tips.kk: A lot of the money goes to middlemen — көмек не үшін керек екенін түсіндіресіз.
tips.ru: A lot of the money goes to middlemen — объясняете, зачем нужна помощь.
tips.example: a lot of the money goes to middlemen

tips.en: So everyone would benefit brings the village and the city together in one conclusion.
tips.kk: So everyone would benefit — қорытынды ауыл мен қаланы біріктіреді.
tips.ru: So everyone would benefit — итог объединяет село и город.

note.en: “Traders between the producer and the buyer”.

questions.question: Should governments help small farmers sell their products directly to the public?

text: I think it should be allowed but controlled. Street sellers make a city feel lively, and for many families it's an important source of income. On the other hand, if there are no rules, pavements get blocked and hygiene can be a real concern, especially with food. So the best approach is probably to give vendors licences and specific places to work.

tips.en: Allowed but controlled states the position in three words.
tips.kk: Allowed but controlled — ұстаным үш сөзбен.
tips.ru: Allowed but controlled — позиция в трёх словах.
tips.example: it should be allowed but controlled

tips.en: Licences and specific places are a concrete measure, not just “something must be done”.
tips.kk: Licences and specific places — «бірдеңе істеу керек» орнына нақты шара.
tips.ru: Licences and specific places — конкретная мера вместо «надо что-то делать».
tips.example: give vendors licences and specific places to work

questions.question: Should street vending be allowed in city centres?

text: Because a market shows you how people really live. In a museum, you see the past, but in a market you see what locals eat, how they talk to each other and what they care about. It's also one of the few places where tourists can try local food cheaply and safely. Personally, whenever I travel, a market is usually the first place I go.

tips.en: In a museum, you see the past — the comparison explains the main idea.
tips.kk: In a museum, you see the past — музеймен салыстыру басты ойды түсіндіреді.
tips.ru: In a museum, you see the past — сравнение с музеем объясняет главную мысль.
tips.example: In a museum, you see the past

tips.en: Whenever I travel adds a short personal experience at the end.
tips.kk: Whenever I travel … — соңында қысқа жеке тәжірибе.
tips.ru: Whenever I travel … — короткий личный опыт в конце.
tips.example: whenever I travel, a market is usually the first place I go
